hypotheses_validated.claim: Scalar, AVX2 and AVX-512 kernels are memcmp-identical for F32/F16/BF16/Q8/Q4, any T, any row range; batched T == T single calls (INV-DET-3, INV-DET-2 at kernel level).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: engine/tests/test_quant.c: 295 matmul cases (rows 1..67, cols 1..4096 float / 64..4096 quant, T 1..9, 7 input kinds incl. zero blocks, outliers, +-max, exact .5 ties, subnormal/tiny, cancellation), random row splits, ldy padding sentinels; all 65536 f16/bf16 bit patterns; 117486 checks, 0 failures under /O2, /Od and /fsanitize=address. dumpbin of quant_avx2.obj / quant_avx512.obj contains no vfmadd/vfmsub/vfnm instructions.

hypotheses_validated.claim: The scalar kernels and quantizers implement docs/NUMERICS.md exactly (not just consistently across ISAs).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_quant.c compares the scalar kernels bitwise to an independent NUMERICS §1-§3 implementation decoded from the FORMAT.md byte layout; helpers (sum16, dot16, rmsnorm, softmax, swiglu, sigmoid, rope, axpy) bitwise vs canonical-order code and within tolerance of float64. Pinned FNV hashes of Q8/Q4 quantizer output and of all five dtypes' matmul output on libm-free inputs were reproduced exactly by an independent numpy/pure-Python implementation (scratch script, not in repo).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Mutation sensitivity: the test detects FMA contraction, wrong reduction tree, wrong mul order, truncating rounding, lane/tail mistakes, nibble swaps, wrong Q4 bias, mask/store errors, quantizer changes and helper-order changes.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: 21 hand-made mutants run against test_quant --no-bench --small during development (7 of them before the final kernel/quantizer restructure, the rest on the final code); 20 killed (1..315 failures each). Two mutants first survived and the test was strengthened until they were killed: rmsnorm eps doubled (added an eps=0.25 case + bitwise canonical checks) and dropping SNaN quieting in the scalar f16 converter (equivalent inside kernels; added a dequantize SNaN bit-pattern check). One earlier mutant (refit tie-break <= in the old refit-every-candidate quantizer) survived as near-equivalent and no longer applies to the current algorithm. Not run through governance/tools/mutate.py (not available yet).

hypotheses_validated.claim: ASAN catches SIMD over-reads in this harness (MSVC instruments intrinsic loads).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Injected a 1-byte over-read in the AVX-512 Q8 unpack: ASAN reported heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 32. Clean code: ASAN run 0 failures, no reports.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Multi-threaded decode over a DRAM-resident matrix approaches the machine's read bandwidth.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Plain AVX-512 streaming read of 1 GiB measured 56 GB/s (1 thread) to 62 GB/s (16-32 threads). Kernels at 16 threads on 1 GiB: 55-60 GB/s for every dtype (AVX-512 and AVX2), i.e. ~90-97% of that ceiling. Measured while other engineers ran builds/tests (CPU 50-100% busy at times): noisy.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Q4 scale search beats a plain absmax/7 baseline on every block and overall.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Per-block squared error <= baseline for all 16384 test blocks; RMSE on N(0,1) 0.08959 vs 0.10756 (16.7% lower, SNR 20.95 vs 19.37 dB). Q8 (absmax/127 per spec) RMSE 0.005925 (44.55 dB).

hypotheses_validated.claim: The maintainers' kernel-level golden test passes with these kernels.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: HEARTH_LIB=<data dir>/build/hxcc/hearth_kernels.dll python -m pytest tests/golden/test_golden_invariants.py -k kernel_isa_and_batch_identity -q -> 5 passed (F32, F16, BF16, Q8, Q4), using T03's python/hearth/_native.py and quant.py as they were at 2026-10-04T13:58Z.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: vpgatherdd is the fastest way to collect the 16 per-row f16 block scales.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Single-core L2 Q4: gather 59 GB/s, 16 scalar loads + pinsrw 76 GB/s, loads packed 4-per-u64 in GPRs then vmovq/vpinsrq 86 GB/s (adopted). Masked per-lane loads were far slower (16-25 GB/s).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Software prefetch improves the DRAM-bound multi-threaded Q4/Q8 kernels.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Prefetch distances 512/1024/2048 bytes (all rows or alternating rows) lowered 16-thread DRAM throughput from ~57 to 52-55 GB/s and single-core L2 from ~84 to ~70 GB/s. Not used.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Least-squares refitting every Q4 candidate is needed for quality.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Refitting only the winner (up to 3 iterations) changed RMSE/rms by < 0.01% on N(0,1), Student-t(4) and Laplace data (e.g. 0.089782 -> 0.089779) at ~1.7x the speed; adopted and documented in quant.c.

open_questions: GCC/Clang builds (Linux/macOS, and the CMake -mavx512* flags) were not compiled here (no gcc/clang on this machine); reviewed by reading only.

Q4 quantizer throughput (~25-40 M weights/s per core, ~400 M/s at 16 threads, noisy) means ~30 min to quantize a 671B model. The arithmetic is plain scalar C by mandate; an SSE2/AVX2 version of the same operations would be bit-identical and several times faster if maintainers allow it.
Float-dtype kernels re-read the row tile per token for T > 1 (fine for routers; a token-blocked variant would help large-T prefill on F16/BF16 weights).
